reference: Metadata expectations use GNU Bash's documented type/help builtins and the published su usage/help contract. The util-linux su executable is not a safe or equivalent oracle for this builtin: its operations authenticate against host account services and change process identity, while bash-os su uses a kernel auth token. No operation parity is claimed.
coverage: Bash reports su as a registered builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented su invocation, password model, and kernel-token description.
Deferred operation coverage identifies parser, account-file, authentication, token, privilege-transition, child-execution, and terminal requirements for a disposable VM or injected mock.
exclusions: No su operation invocation is run. Authentication, token authorization, credential changes, target-shell execution, and PTY behavior require controlled private fixtures or a disposable VM.
No host account, password, shadow file, authorization device, or installed credential is accessed.
No GNU/util-linux su comparison is run because it would use host authentication and identity-changing behavior and does not implement the bash-os token contract.

cases.purpose: Verify that Bash resolves su as a builtin using the documented type -t metadata contract, without invoking su.

Check that the registered help text contains the declared invocation form and documented password and auth-token descriptions. The fixed marker is emitted only when all documented anchors are present.
cases.script:
PATH=
help su >help.txt
want_usage='su [--login|--no-login] [--keep-env] [-c CMD] [USER]'
usage=0
description=0
password=0
token=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  case $line in
    *"$want_usage"*) usage=1 ;;
    *'Switch user with C-owned password verification.'*) description=1 ;;
    *'Argon2id PHC shadow format used by passwd.'*) password=1 ;;
    *'short-lived kernel auth token is minted and consumed internally'*) token=1 ;;
  esac
done <help.txt
[[ $usage == 1 && $description == 1 && $password == 1 && $token == 1 ]]
printf 'help contract anchors present\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise option parsing, default target selection, --, -c forms, extra arguments, invalid names, and exit/diagnostic behavior.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or parser-focused injected harness with a private synthetic passwd database. Normal valid invocation forks into authentication and privilege-transition paths, so no operation command is run here.

cases.purpose: Check account lookup for present, absent, malformed, and unreadable synthetic passwd records, including target UID/GID/home/shell selection.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed account-file syscall mock with private passwd data and injected file-open errors. It must not consult installed accounts or change account state.

cases.purpose: Check correct and incorrect passwords, locked or malformed shadow entries, bounded password input, failure lockout, and success cleanup.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private PTY, synthetic PHC shadow records, an independent Argon2id oracle, private lock files and injected password-read outcomes. No installed credentials or host shadow data may be used.

cases.purpose: Check token mint/consume request fields, expiry, failure handling, and request cleanup before any credential transition.
cases.reason: Requires an independently reviewed mock for /dev/bashos-auth in a disposable VM or syscall fixture. The live authority device and kernel authorization are not exercised.

cases.purpose: Check supplementary groups and ordered setgroups/setresgid/setresuid transitions, saved-ID verification, and denial on each injected failure.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or syscall mock that records and injects credential syscalls. This suite must not attempt a real user or group change.

cases.purpose: Check login and no-login argv, working directory, filtered and retained environment, descriptor closure, and exec errors using a controlled target shell.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed credential/token syscall mock with a private synthetic account and a fixture shell executable that records argv, environment, cwd and inherited descriptors. No installed shell is launched through su in this suite.

cases.purpose: Check child exit and signal status propagation, fork/wait errors, parent-shell state preservation, and repeated invocation behavior.
cases.reason: Requires a bounded disposable child-process fixture with mocked authentication and credential operations. Any signals must target only owned fixture children; this suite sends none.

cases.purpose: Check tty password echo suppression and terminal restoration after success, read failure, and cancellation.
cases.reason: Requires a private PTY driver, deterministic password input, and a mockable child/auth path in a disposable VM. No interactive su session is started here.
